extractions.value: The dalakas criteria are used worldwide to diagnose SPS. Following five are the components of the criteria.[1] Stiffness in the axial muscles, prominently in the abdominal and thoracolumbar paraspinal muscles leading to a fixed deformity (hyperlordosis). [2] Superimposed painful spasms precipitated by unexpected noises, emotional stress, tactile stimuli.[3] Confirmation of the continuous motor unit activity in agonist and antagonist muscles by electromyography.[4] Absence of neurological impairments that could explain the stiffness. [5] Positive serology for GAD65 (or amphiphysin) autoantibodies, assessed by immunocytochemistry, western blot or radioimmunoassay. Reported child had 4 out of 5 parameters of the above criteria. We could not do electromyogram.
